description: Part 1: Perform extensive EDA on Final_data.csv with comprehensive visualizations and statistical analysis. Part 2: Generate 5 million rows of synthetic data and verify only row count and null values.

file_info.description: Source CSV file for analysis and synthetic data generation

part_1_extensive_eda.description: Comprehensive exploratory data analysis with extensive visualizations and professional web report
requirements: Perform extensive EDA on ALL columns with thorough statistical analysis
Generate ALL possible plots and save them in an 'eda_plots' folder
Create individual plot files for: distributions, correlations, outliers, relationships, patterns, trends
Include univariate analysis (histograms, box plots, violin plots, KDE plots for numeric columns)
Include bivariate analysis (scatter plots, correlation heatmaps, pair plots for top correlations)
Include categorical analysis (bar charts, pie charts, count plots, cross-tabulations)
Include advanced visualizations (3D plots if applicable, interactive plots, cluster visualizations)
Perform statistical tests and save results
Create a staging data file 'report_data.json' containing ALL analysis results, statistics, and plot references
Build a professional HTML report with separate files: 'eda_report.html', 'eda_report.css', 'eda_report.js'
The HTML file should load data from 'report_data.json' using JavaScript
CSS should provide modern, responsive styling with good UX (cards, tabs, collapsible sections, smooth animations)
JavaScript should handle data loading, dynamic content generation, interactive features, and plot embedding
The report should be fully functional as a standalone web application
Make the analysis as thorough and detailed as possible - explore every aspect of the data
part_1_extensive_eda.workflow: Step 1: Create 'eda_plots' folder. Step 2: Generate and save ALL individual plots (PNG/SVG). Step 3: Perform statistical analysis. Step 4: Create 'report_data.json' with all analysis results and plot paths. Step 5: Create 'eda_report.css' with modern styling. Step 6: Create 'eda_report.js' to load data and generate content. Step 7: Create 'eda_report.html' that ties everything together.
part_1_extensive_eda.output: Professional web-based EDA report with separate HTML/CSS/JS files, 'report_data.json' staging file, and 'eda_plots' folder with all visualizations

part_2_synthetic_generation.description: Generate 5M synthetic rows with minimal validation
instructions: Use the analysis from Part 1 to understand data structure
Use simple sequential batch generation (100k rows per batch)
NO multiprocessing, NO multithreading to avoid timeouts

checks_only: Check for null values in each column

part_2_synthetic_generation.output: synthetic_data_5m.parquet and simple validation report (row count + null check only)

execution_preferences.reasoning: Part 1 (EDA) must complete first. Part 2 (generation) uses Part 1 results. Simple sequential processing to avoid timeouts.

part_1_outputs: eda_report.css - Styling for the report (modern, responsive design)
eda_report.js - JavaScript for data loading and interactivity
report_data.json - Staging file with all analysis results, statistics, and plot paths
eda_plots/ - Folder containing all individual plot files (PNG/SVG)
part_2_outputs: validation_summary.json - Simple validation (row count and null values only)

critical_instructions.for_eda: WORKFLOW: Step 1: Create 'eda_plots' folder and generate ALL plots incrementally (PNG/SVG format). Step 2: Perform statistical analysis. Step 3: Create 'report_data.json' with all results (dataset overview, column stats, plot paths, correlations, insights). Step 4: Create 'eda_report.css' with modern responsive design (use CSS Grid/Flexbox, cards, tabs, smooth animations). Step 5: Create 'eda_report.js' to fetch report_data.json and dynamically generate content (handle data loading, plot embedding, interactive features). Step 6: Create 'eda_report.html' as a clean shell that loads CSS and JS. The report should work as a standalone web app with professional UX.
critical_instructions.for_validation: Keep validation MINIMAL - only check row count (must be 5M) and null values. Do NOT perform distribution comparisons, correlation analysis, or statistical tests.
